newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: U.S. jobs data showed more weakness than expected, causing an already strong Swiss bond market to surge late in the day.
News September payrolls fell by 40,000, compared with forecasts for 166,000 rise, caused U.S. Treasuries to soar.
December Swiss Confederate bond futures hit a contract high of 115.74 late in the day. It was also the highest level for the lead-month Conf on a continuation basis so far this year.
The Swiss National Bank's average yield of government paper, which includes maturities of at least five years, was calculated at 3.66 percent at midday, a new low for the year.

Matthias Weber, analyst at Bank Leu, said the market appeared to be "very euphoric," and did not rule out some correction. But, he also said it was possible that 10-year government yields could remain below the key 4.00 percent level for a while, perhaps a couple of months.
With 10-year yields at roughly 3.80 percent, he did not expect further significant price gains. But he also did not expect any sharp correction, given that the Swiss economy remained weak.
The latest signs of weakness in the U.S. economy should also give Swiss bonds some support.
Traders said volume was relatively high even before the release of the U.S. numbers.
"We had continuous high volume with the focus on the long end," said one bond trader at a Swiss bank.
He said demand was also fairly broad.

In the short end, money market rates were also seen slightly lower in the afternoon. But they remained somewhat tight a week after the Swiss National Bank cut its discount rate to 1.00 percent from 1.50 percent. One trader said demand from one large bank may have been enough to keep overnight rates closer to 1.50 percent than 1.00 percent.
Dec conf futures CONFZ6 up 53 at 115.65.
Dec comi medium-term bond COMIZ6 up 24 at 110.66
Dec Euro Swiss francs FESZ6 unchanged at 98.44.
